articles.title: Why oil prices haven't gone crazy despite 5 months of US-Iran war
articles.summary: Oil prices remained relatively stable despite five months of US-Iran conflict, peaking at $126 per barrel—well below the 2008 high of $147. Brent crude averaged $101 between February 28 and June 11, when the US called off strikes, before dropping to $70 in early July. The conflict raises concerns for India, a major oil importer, due to potential supply disruptions and price volatility affecting fuel costs and inflation.

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds removal of commercial activity from elephant corridor
articles.summary: The Supreme Court upheld a 2011 Madras High Court order that declared the Segur Plateau Elephant Corridor in Tamil Nadu as a protected area free from commercial activities. The ruling resolves a long-standing dispute over the corridor's status and reinforces environmental protection measures for elephant habitats. The Tamil Nadu government had notified the corridor in 2011, but commercial activities had persisted, leading to legal challenges.
